thread:
alex: Quick RFC follow-up — we landed the per-route retry budget sketch but we didn’t settle how SDKs should surface it across Python/TS/Go. My proposal: a small, composable RetryBudget object that can be attached to a client route or an iterator. Default is global, opt-in per-route. Thoughts?

maria: +1 to composable. Curious about ergonomics for paginated iterators — do we drain budget per page request or per item returned?

jordan: Important distinction. For our workloads (embedding batches + long pages) budget should be consumed per RPC, not per item. Otherwise a single large page can exhaust tokens unexpectedly.

sam: Agreed. Also we need clear semantics when a streaming response (long-poll) is downgraded to paged fallback. Does the iterator inherit the stream's budget or get a fresh one?

priya: My vote: inherit in a transparent way. If a streamed call fails and we fall back to pages, the iterator should keep remaining tokens from the original call to avoid double-charging. But API must make it explicit so callers can reason about it.

alex: Implementation note: SDK shape examples below — open to shorter names. Python:

```
client = RedwoodClient(retry_budget=RetryBudget(window_s=60, tokens=50))
# per-route override
client.chat.set_route('streaming', RetryBudget(tokens=10))
# iterator uses the route's budget
for chunk in client.chat.stream(...).iterator(reuse_budget=True):
    ...
```

TS:

```
const client = new RedwoodClient({ retryBudget: { windowSec: 60, tokens: 50 } });
client.chat.route('streaming').withRetryBudget({ tokens: 10 });
for await (const page of client.chat.stream(...).pages({ inheritBudget: true })) {
  // pages consume RPC tokens
}
```

Go:

```
cli := redwood.NewClient(redwood.WithRetryBudget(redwood.RetryBudget{WindowSec:60,Tokens:50}))
cli.Chat.Route("streaming").SetRetryBudget(redwood.RetryBudget{Tokens:10})
it := cli.Chat.Stream(...).Iterator() // Iterator uses route budget by default
```

jordan: API sketch looks ok. A few tradeoffs:
- Default: iterator consumes per-RPC (not per-item).
- Expose a low-level hook so advanced callers can charge budget manually (useful for custom prefetch).
- Need telemetry emits when budgets are inherited vs created so Console can surface confusing cases.

maria: Backoff interplay — do we treat budget tokens as "attempts" or "cost units"? If attempt-based then exponential backoff retries could blow through tokens quickly. If cost-units, we can weight retries by expected token cost.

alex: Good catch. I prefer cost-units. Each RPC has an estimated cost (based on average page size or token estimate). Retry consumes cost proportional to expected retry work. That also lets us prioritize canary vs best-effort routes.

sam: For streaming->paged fallback, implement a tiny in-memory lease: the stream holds N tokens reserved; on fallback, remaining lease transfers to the iterator. ops-bot can emit a lease-transfer event.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: Canary rollout of retry-budget v1 scheduled Thu 11:00 PT. Monitoring: budget_exhausted, budget_inherit, lease_transfer.

priya: One more: serializer surface — keep route config declarative and language idiomatic. E.g., Python use objects, TS use POJOs, Go use structs. Avoid callbacks for budget semantics.

jordan: Also add a simple one-liner helper to reset budget state for testing, e.g., client.testing.resetRetryBudget(route) so tests are deterministic.

alex: Action items: 1) I’ll update RFC to use "cost units" and include the three SDK sketches. 2) @maria can you add Console telemetry events mapping? 3) @sam can you prototype lease-transfer for streaming fallback? 4) @priya write small ergonomics notes for each SDK.

maria: Ack — will sketch telemetry in the Console doc and link to the rollout.

sam: Will prototype this week, ping me if you want to pair on edge cases.

priya: I’ll draft language-specific examples and throw them into the SDK repo README.

alex: Thanks all. If nobody objects I’ll flip the RFC to implement next sprint. :rocket:
